findings.title: Paged subgroup listing still dereferences a possibly-null model
findings.body: getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) calls modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. The supplier resolves to null when another request has deleted the group, which is the race this PR targets, so this still throws the same NPE. The same unguarded pattern appears at lines 262 and 268 in the other two paged overloads. Only getSubGroupsCount was guarded, so the reported bug is only partly fixed.

findings.title: Deleted group silently reports a null subgroup count
findings.body: The NPE is replaced by returning null from a method whose contract is a count. The missing group is swallowed here and the null propagates into representations (populateSubGroupCount assigns it directly). Callers that unbox the Long or compare it will now throw NPE far from the cause. Other methods in this adapter throw IllegalStateException('Not found in database') when the group is gone, so behavior is inconsistent. Pick one defined behavior and document it on GroupModel.

findings.title: Null guard in getRoleMappings tests the supplier instead of the group
findings.body: The check 'if (group == null)' tests the Supplier<GroupModel> parameter. GroupAdapter always passes its non-null modelSupplier, so the guard never fires. When the underlying group has been deleted, the supplier returns null, and that null reaches the lazy loader. The comment describes exactly the case this guard was meant to handle, so the intended protection is missing and the PR does not address it. The check should be on group.get() == null before calling the loader.

findings.title: getAttributes and getSubGroups have no null handling for a deleted group
findings.body: Unlike getRoleMappings, getAttributes (lines 66-68) and getSubGroups (lines 90-92) pass the supplier straight to DefaultLazyLoader. The loaders at lines 55 and 57 dereference the source (source.getAttributes(), source.getSubGroupsStream()). Assuming the loader runs on the supplied source when the value is not yet loaded, a group deleted before its first attribute or subgroup access makes the supplier return null and the loader throws NPE. That affects getFirstAttribute, getAttributes, getAttributeStream and getSubGroupsStream() in GroupAdapter, so the concurrent NPE remains reachable.

findings.title: Parent lookup result used without a null check during hierarchy build
findings.body: session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId()) returns null if the parent was deleted between listing and this lookup. parentModel is then passed to groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel) at line 51 (when admin permissions are off), to toRepresentation inside computeIfAbsent at line 57, and to populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, parent) at line 60, which calls getSubGroupsCount() on null. This is the same concurrent-deletion NPE in the group listing path, and the PR edits this file without handling it. A null check that drops the orphaned child or skips the parent is needed.

findings.title: Reader thread is not joined, so late failures are ignored
findings.body: deletedAll is set and the assertion runs at line 157 without joining the reader thread started at line 139. The reader may still be inside an in-flight request, and any exception it records after the assertion is evaluated is never checked. The test can therefore pass despite the failure it is meant to catch. The thread should be joined, with a timeout, before asserting.

findings.title: Exception during deletion leaves a non-daemon busy-looping thread running
findings.body: If group(...).remove() at line 153 throws (for example a 500 from the bug under test), the exception escapes the forEach and deletedAll.set(true) at line 155 never runs. The reader thread (lines 139-149) then loops forever issuing HTTP requests. As a non-daemon thread it also keeps the JVM alive, so the run hangs instead of failing cleanly. The flag should be set in a finally block, and the reader should be a daemon or be stopped explicitly.

findings.title: Race-based test may not reproduce the NPE and has no deterministic interleaving
findings.body: The NPE requires a cached adapter with a loaded group, a concurrent deletion, and then a lazy access. This test depends on timing between one reader thread and 100 sequential deletes, and it only asserts that no exception reached the client. Nothing shows it fails on the base commit, so it may pass without the fix. The author should confirm it reproduces the failure without the change, or drive the interleaving deterministically (for example by deleting the group on the server between the read and the access).

findings.title: Reader thread spins on HTTP requests with no pause
findings.body: The reader loop at lines 139-149 issues back-to-back list requests over 100 groups for the whole deletion phase with no sleep or backoff. This saturates the shared test server, slows the test, and adds load that can cause timeouts on CI. A short pause between iterations would avoid this.
